test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In basketball, a player must release the ball within how many seconds when attempting a free throw?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 seconds**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Official Basketball Rules** established by **FIBA** (International Basketball Federation) and the **NBA** (National Basketball Association), a player must release the ball within **10 seconds** when attempting a **free throw**.
 
• The **10-second count** begins as soon as the **official** or **referee** places the ball at the **disposal** of the shooter at the **free-throw line**.
 
• If the player fails to release the ball within this **time limit**, a **violation** is called. This results in the **cancellation** of the shot (if it goes in) and the ball being awarded to the **opposing team** for a **throw-in** from the **sideline**, provided no further free throws are pending.
 
• This rule is designed to maintain the **pace of the game** and prevent players from using the **free-throw line** as an opportunity for excessive **rest** or **stalling**.
 
• The option of **5 seconds** is incorrect for free throws; however, it is a critical **numerical value** used for **inbounding** the ball or when a player is **closely guarded** in the frontcourt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **24-Second Shot Clock**: Introduced in **1954** by **Danny Biasone**, this rule requires a team to attempt a **field goal** that touches the **rim** within **24 seconds** of gaining **possession**.
 
• **8-Second Rule**: Once a team gains possession in their **backcourt**, they must advance the ball into the **frontcourt** within **8 seconds**. Failure to do so results in a **turnover**.
 
• **3-Second Rule**: An **offensive player** is prohibited from remaining in the **opposing team's restricted area** (the **paint** or **key**) for more than **3 consecutive seconds** while their team has the ball.
 
• **5-Second Closely Guarded Rule**: In **international basketball** and **college basketball**, a player who is **closely guarded** (within **one meter**) must pass, shoot, or dribble the ball within **5 seconds**.
 
• **Scoring**: Unlike **field goals** which are worth **2 or 3 points**, each successful **free throw** adds exactly **1 point** to the team's total score.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Court Dimensions**: The **free-throw line** is located at a distance of **15 feet** (approximately **4.57 meters**) from the plane of the **backboard**.
 
• **Invention of the Game**: Basketball was invented by **Dr. James Naismith** in **December 1891** in **Springfield, Massachusetts**, **USA**. The **free throw** was officially introduced in **1894**.
 
• **Penalty/Bonus Situation**: When a team exceeds the limit of **4 team fouls** in a **quarter** (in the **NBA**), the opposing team enters the **bonus** and receives **two free throws** for every subsequent non-shooting foul.
 
• **Lane Alignment**: During a **free throw** attempt, a maximum of **five players** (three defensive and two offensive) may occupy the **lane spaces** to compete for a **rebound** if the shot is missed.
